title: Nanoscape: The Journal for Undergraduate Research in Nanoscience
description: Nanoscape: The Journal for Undergraduate Research in Nanoscience is an annual publication of original research conducted by undergraduates from around the county. The journal was launched in 2004 and was the first of its kind in the country. The journal disseminates the results of undergraduate research in the broad fields of nanoscience and nanotechnology. Nanoscape is an educational outreach project of the Northwestern University Nanoscale Science and Engineering Center (NSEC), which is part of the International Institute for Nanotechnology (IIN), both of which are under the direction of Professor Chad A. Mirkin. This work was supported primarily by the Nanoscale Science and Engineering Initiative of the National Science Foundation Under NSF award number EEC–0755375 AND EEC-0647560.

title: Calculations on the Optical Properties of Layered Metal Nanospheres
creator: Kevin Shuford
John Flintermann
George Schatz
description:
In this experiment, the optical properties
of several spherical nanoparticles were
observed. Particles were modeled using
Mie theory, a set of equations that calculate
the extinction coefficient of virtually any
spherical particle. Initially this theory was
used to model solid particles made of noble
metals. As time passed, its scope was
broadened to modeling coated nanospheres
and other different materials. We attempted
to observe many trends among the particles
while changing their composition, core
size, and shell size. We found that by subtly
changing the attributes of the particles, we
could significantly modify their extinction
spectra. Finally, we attempted to model socalled
“whispering-gallery modes” using
Mie theory. The theory was able to predict
their absorption and scattering effectively,
but the programs employed were unable to
model large, highly absorbing spheres.
